judgments.reasoning_cat1: The parenthetical states that any additional benefit provision attached to the policy will terminate according to its terms 'unless otherwise provided' — an open-ended saving phrase whose source and reach are not identified. The amount of paid-up insurance is also left blank, so the operative election is incomplete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with the separate election to cancel Supplementary Agreements (c015) and with the release on cancellation of any part of the policy (c020), so which mechanism governs the termination of riders is not clearly allocated among the three.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: This is standard tax-notice language warning that the owner remains liable for federal income tax on the taxable portion and may face estimated tax penalties; it imposes no contractual obligation to construe. The text is scrambled by OCR but its sense is conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits consistently with the withholding instructions (c010) and the box A/B elections (c014, c016) and contradicts nothing in the form.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause says future monthly insurance costs will be charged based on the reduced or removed rating, which is a determinate consequence once the box is ticked. 'Rating' is a term of art but not one carrying competing meanings here.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It presupposes a cost-of-insurance schedule in the underlying universal life policy that is not part of this instrument, but no provision in the form conflicts with it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single election sentence declining federal income tax withholding on the distribution; its meaning is fixed and standard. Nothing to name as ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches box A as described in the instructions (c010) and is qualified, consistently, by the default 20% rule in c017.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause cancels 'the following Supplementary Agreement(s)' with the list left blank, so what is cancelled cannot be determined from the text — an enumerated-list scope problem in its purest form. The undefined label 'Supplementary Agreement' compounds it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with the paid-up insurance parenthetical (c011), which independently terminates additional benefit provisions, and with the release clause (c020) governing the consequences of cancelling part of the policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line election to have federal income tax withheld from the distribution; determinate and standard. No ambiguous term to identify.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It corresponds to box B in the instructions (c010) and is consistent with the tax notice (c012).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence imposes a 20% default withholding where the owner's Social Security number is not completed; the rule is mechanical and its trigger objectively verifiable. The OCR damage does not create competing meanings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies the box A election (c014) in the ordinary way rather than contradicting it, and fits the instructions in c010.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The representation runs to 'no bankruptcy proceedings, attachment, tax or other lien claim pending against me', a specific list closed by a general catch-all whose reach ('other lien claim') is uncertain, and 'pending' is itself open. That is a nameable general-versus-specific tension, though in a short warranty of limited consequence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the form addresses creditors, attachments or liens, so there is no counterpart provision with which it can conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause makes acceptance of a policy or policy change a ratification of any correction or change 'made by and noted under Home Office Endorsement above', yet in the same breath says there can be no change in amount, age at issue, risk, plan or benefits unless the owner agrees in writing — a deemed-ratification-by-conduct rule set directly against a written-agreement-only rule. The scope of 'any correction or change' against that carve-out list is precisely what two parties would read differently.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Home Office Endorsement block on this same form endorses a change 'by attachment' effective December 1995 signed only by the company's president and secretary, so the endorsement machinery and the writing requirement in this clause point in opposite directions on the very change the form effects (see also the amount change in c006).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause releases Ohio National 'from any claims or liability under such part' if any part of the policy is cancelled by a change, and then says premium adjustments 'will then be made' — both 'part' and the adjustment mechanism are undefined, and the release is drafted wholly in the insurer's favour so any genuine ambiguity would be read against it. The truncated final sentence leaves the adjustment obligation without a stated measure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be squared with the cancellation election (c015), the paid-up insurance parenthetical (c011) which says riders terminate 'according to its terms unless otherwise provided', and the writing requirement in c019; whether a company-initiated endorsement can trigger this release is not resolved by the instrument.
